pages.text: The Workstation turns warehouse elements into items, and breaks warehouse items back down into elements. Breaking down returns only a fraction of what the item cost to make, so it is for clearing out stock you have no use for, not for profit.
The Workstation turns elements into items, or breaks them back down

Both directions only touch the town warehouse — nothing in your own inventory is involved. When a shop runs short, the Workstation gets called in automatically to craft the missing goods, so seeing it start a job on its own is normal.

A Workstation works on one job at a time, so anything queued behind it waits its turn. If crafting feels slow, build a second one somewhere else — each keeps its own queue and they can run at once. Mages do the actual work, though, so extra Workstations add nothing $(br)while every mage is busy.

A new town has none of its crafting recipes unlocked, and the greyed-out half of the list on the Synthesize tab is exactly that. There are three ways to open one: deposit an item into the warehouse and its own recipe unlocks with it;
pages.title: Unlocking Recipes

pages.text: hold a wand and right-click a block in Identify mode to unlock that block's recipe on the spot; or take an $(l:wandscape:items/blueprint_guide)Item Blueprint$(/l) and pick any single recipe on the Recipes page in the warehouse. Unlocks are per town and permanent.
